subject: Renewal discussion: retain + scale — concession matrix proposal
messages:
From: Sofia Vega <s.vega@nimbusretail.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-12T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal planning — upcoming term and capacity ask

Alex — thanks for the heads up in last week's call. Renewal for Nimbus is approaching (term ends 2027-07-31). We expect Q3 usage to grow ~35% with a new personalization pilot and a planned EU rollout later in the year.

Priority asks from our side:
- Can you hold current unit rates for 6 months while we ramp (price-hold)?
- We need a committed capacity increase (roughly +40%) but want some flexibility on true-ups for the first quarter.
- Looking for a commercial concession (discount or credits) to offset migration and integration costs.

Timing: procurement needs a proposed term sheet by next Wednesday (2027-05-19). Can you share what options you can offer?

Thanks —
Sofia
Head of Platform Partnerships
Nimbus Retail
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-12T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Renewal planning — upcoming term and capacity ask

Folks — forwarding Nimbus' note. High level: they want a 6-month price hold while they ramp + a ~40% committed capacity bump and credits for migration. Procurement deadline is 5/19.

Can you sketch a pragmatic concession matrix we can offer that balances economics + ops? Key constraints: my manager is incentivized to protect ASP; finance wants clear commit math; we should preserve an option for staged true-up vs immediate committed uplift.

Cc'ing no one else yet; want an internal quick draft.
— Alex
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-13T08:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal planning — upcoming term and capacity ask

Alex / Priyom — rough proposal below (for 5/19 deliverable). I'm keeping all numbers illustrative; Priyom can finalize the sheet: 

Option A (Conservative):
- 12-month renewal; commit = current commit + 25% (phased increase over 3 months)
- 12% list discount on model tokens (applied to baseline commit)
- Price-hold: guarantee current rates for first 4 months post-renewal
- One-time integration credit = $35,000 applied to first invoice

Option B (Aggressive / retention + upsell):
- 12-month renewal; commit = current commit + 40% (immediate)
- 18% list discount on committed usage; overage at 60% of list rate
- Price-hold: 6 months on committed unit price
- Onboarding credit = $50,000 + 2 months complimentary burst capacity (up to 50% over commit)
- Legal: include EU carveout clause (EU region billed at parity but separate true-up)

Operational notes: require a 30-day notice to reduce commit after month 3; staged true-up (quarterly) for actuals vs commit.

If they accept Option B we get stronger committed revenue and a cleaner uplift; Option A is lower risk. Recommend we present both and push for B. Priyom: can you run the P&L and updated commit calc and attach?

—Marissa
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Vega <s.vega@nimbusretail.com>, Mark Liu <mark.liu@nimbusretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-14T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Nimbus renewal — proposed concession matrix and term sheet (draft)

Sofia / Mark — thanks again for the conversation. Attached is a short term sheet and a commit calculator (Redwood-Commit-Calc.xlsx) with two commercial options for your review: Option A (conservative) and Option B (retention + scale). Key highlights:

- Option B (recommended): 12-month term, +40% commit, 18% discount on committed tokens, 6-month price-hold on committed unit price, $50k one-time onboarding credit, and 2 months of complimentary burst.
- EU rollout: we propose a separate EU carveout (same list rates but separate true-up cadence) to address data residency/regulatory concerns.
- Delivery: we can finalize legal redlines within 5 business days once commercial terms are agreed.

Attachments: Nimbus_Renewal_Term_Sheet_v3.pdf; Redwood-Commit-Calc.xlsx

Next steps: can you confirm (1) preferred option or (2) the specific items you want to negotiate (price-hold length, credit quantum, EU carveout)? Procurement timeline noted — happy to iterate quickly.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
From: Mark Liu <mark.liu@nimbusretail.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Sofia Vega <s.vega@nimbusretail.com>
Date: 2027-05-17T15:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Nimbus renewal — proposed concession matrix and term sheet (draft)

Thanks Alex — reviewed with procurement and finance. A few asks / counterpoints: 

- Price-hold: 9 months would be ideal for us given product launch risk. Can you extend to 9 months on Option B?
- Burst: Can the 2 months complimentary burst be expanded to 3 months, and can the burst capacity be up to 75% of commit for month 1?
- EU carveout: we need price parity but require separate invoicing and the ability to true-up independently for EU usage. Can you confirm this is acceptable?
- Credit: can the onboarding credit be structured as a $40k credit + $20k implementation services credit (applied to professional services line) — this helps align to our SOW.

On quoting cadence: procurement needs a near-final commercial redline by 5/19. If we can't get 9 months, can you confirm the maximum price-hold you can commit to and any tradeoffs?

On Wed, May 14, 2027 at 11:22 AM Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com> wrote:
> Sofia / Mark — thanks again for the conversation. Attached is a short term sheet and a commit calculator (Redwood-Commit-Calc.xlsx) with two commercial options for your review: Option A (conservative) and Option B (retention + scale).

Regards,
Mark Liu
Head of Procurement (Nimbus)
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-20T16:40:00-07:00
Subject: Nimbus counter — internal approval ask (deal DL-2027-0984)

Marissa / Priyom — update from Mark: they counter with requests for a 9-month price-hold, 3 months burst (75% for month 1), and restructured credits ($40k commercial + $20k PS). They also require EU invoicing/true-up separation.

Ask: can we deliver 9 months price-hold on Option B if we (a) reduce the list discount to 16% and (b) make the 3rd month of burst conditional on meeting month-2 commit? Also confirm whether the $20k PS credit is acceptable (applied to professional services only).

Impact: reducing discount to 16% with a 9-month hold and conditional burst keeps unit economics > threshold and preserves incremental committed revenue. If we proceed, I'll send a revised term sheet and request legal to prepare a separate EU annex.

Please respond by EOD 5/21 — procurement expects near-final terms.

— Alex
